claim.pdf_says: In BOTH MULTIPLY general formats the ON SIZE ERROR block is printed as: [| ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1 |] / [| NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2 |], where SIZE, ERROR, NOT and END-MULTIPLY carry underlines but the word ON does NOT (verified by a 900-dpi render; underline strokes sit under SIZE and under ERROR, and under NOT on the second line, with clear white space under both occurrences of ON).
claim.markdown_says: Figure note for Format 1: "`MULTIPLY`, `BY`, `ON`, `SIZE`, `ERROR`, `NOT`, and `END-MULTIPLY` are underlined in the printed standard (required words)." Figure note for Format 2: "`MULTIPLY`, `BY`, `GIVING`, `ON`, `SIZE`, `ERROR`, `NOT`, and `END-MULTIPLY` are underlined in the printed standard (required words)."
claim.why_it_matters: The code-block figures carry no underlining, so these notes are the ONLY carrier of the required/optional word distinction on this page. Listing `ON` as underlined makes it a required word, which would reject the legal statements `MULTIPLY A BY B SIZE ERROR ...` and `MULTIPLY A BY B NOT SIZE ERROR ...`. This is exactly the falsely-restrictive direction the reconciliation is hunting: legal COBOL made to look illegal. The same defect is duplicated in both notes on the page.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by independent inspection, and the claim's quotations of both sources are exact.

1) MARKDOWN QUOTES VERIFIED VERBATIM. E:/Temp/specrecon/v703/page-703.md lines 29-30 and 49-50 read exactly as quoted, including `ON` in both underlined-word lists.

2) PDF INSPECTED DIRECTLY, TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS.
   (a) Vector geometry. The ISO PDF text layer is obfuscated (reference_spec_encoding), so text extraction is useless here, but the underlines are real vector rectangles and were extracted with PyMuPDF get_drawings(). The thin horizontal strokes on page 703 (PDF user-space points) are:
       Format 1: y=267.60 x=[87.96,134.65] (MULTIPLY) and x=[221.95,232.22] (BY);
                 y=301.68 x=[123.91,142.35] and x=[148.65,179.23]  -- only TWO strokes on the "ON SIZE ERROR" line;
                 y=318.95 x=[106.64,124.84], x=[147.72,166.16], x=[169.20,202.11] -- only THREE strokes on the "NOT ON SIZE ERROR" line;
                 y=338.09 x=[102.20,172.93] (END-MULTIPLY).
       Format 2: y=418.86 (MULTIPLY, BY); y=447.81 x=[93.10,124.38] (GIVING); y=470.22 two strokes; y=487.72 three strokes; y=506.63 (END-MULTIPLY).
     Both size-error lines are one stroke short of the word count, and the stroke width ratios match SIZE:ERROR (18.44:30.58 = 1.66 vs. the metric prediction 1.67) and NOT:SIZE:ERROR, not any hypothesis that includes ON. The strokes at y=288.84/320.35 and y=457.38/489.12 are the short top/bottom arms of the enclosing brackets (x approx 93 and 323), not underlines.
   (b) Visual render at 1200 dpi. Cropped E:/Temp/specrecon/v703/fmt1_line1.png, fmt1_line2.png and fmt2_block.png and looked at the glyphs. What I see, unambiguously at that magnification: line 1 reads "ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1" with a rule beneath SIZE and a separate rule beneath ERROR, and clean white space beneath O and N; line 2 reads "NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2" with rules beneath NOT, SIZE and ERROR, and clean white space beneath the intervening ON. Format 2 is identical, with GIVING additionally ruled. Both occurrences of ON in each format -- four in total on the page -- are unruled.

3) NOT A FORMATTING OR REFLOW ARTEFACT. The disputed text is not reflowed, wrapped or page-broken; it is an editorial assertion in the transcription that contradicts the printed page. It inverts the required/optional status of a word, which is exactly the normative distinction 5.2.6 assigns to underlining, so it changes meaning.

4) THE TRANSCRIPTION'S OWN CONVENTION CONFIRMS IT. For the identical construct elsewhere the markdown already records the correct reading: SUBTRACT (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 32089, 32106, 32121) states "...are underlined in the printed standard (required words); `ON` is printed without an underline in both size-error lines", and USE Format 1 (line 32558) likewise lists `ON` among the words "printed without underlining". Section 14.7.5 is titled "SIZE ERROR phrase", not "ON SIZE ERROR phrase". The MULTIPLY notes are the outlier, not the SUBTRACT ones.

5) SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THE PAGE. The same defect exists in the three DIVIDE figure notes at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 26640, 26661 and 26681, which also list `ON` among the underlined words. The page-703 fix should be swept across those siblings in the same change set.

The claim is accurate as written; the only refinement is that the underlined-word lists are otherwise correct (MULTIPLY, BY, GIVING, SIZE, ERROR, NOT, END-MULTIPLY all genuinely carry underlines), so `ON` is the sole erroneous entry in each note.
verdict.corrected_description: Both MULTIPLY figure notes on page 703 wrongly list `ON` as underlined. Verified at 1200 dpi and by extracting the underline rectangles from the PDF vector layer: in Format 1 and Format 2 alike, the printed standard rules MULTIPLY, BY, (GIVING in Format 2), NOT, SIZE, ERROR and END-MULTIPLY, but leaves BOTH occurrences of ON unruled in each format -- four unruled ONs on the page. Each size-error line carries exactly one fewer underline stroke than it has reserved words, and the stroke widths match SIZE and ERROR (and NOT), not ON. Because the markdown code-block figures carry no underlining, the note is the sole carrier of the required/optional distinction, so this makes the optional word ON look required and would falsely reject the legal `MULTIPLY A BY B SIZE ERROR ...` and `MULTIPLY A BY B NOT SIZE ERROR ...`. Fix: drop `ON` from both lists and, matching the convention already used for SUBTRACT (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 32089/32106/32121) and USE (line 32558), append "; `ON` is printed without an underline in both size-error lines". The identical defect is present in the three DIVIDE figure notes at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 26640, 26661 and 26681 and should be swept in the same change set.
